newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung in takeover talk with Ssangyong Motor - govt.
newsitem.headline: Samsung in takeover talk with Ssangyong Motor - govt.

text.p: South Korea's trade ministry said on Friday Samsung Motors Inc, a unit of Samsung Group, is in talks to take over Ssangyong Motor Co Ltd.
"I understand the two companies are now talking. Basically, the government has no reason to object a voluntary takeover between private companies," Trade Minister Ahn Kwang-koo said.
A ministry statement quoted Ahn as telling local reporters that the government would neither help nor block such a deal.

There has been widespread speculation that Samsung tries to take over loss-making Ssangyong Motor. Samsung, which is setting up an automobile plant with a technical tie-up with Nissan Motor Co of Japan, plans to start rolling out cars in 1998.
Ssangyong Motor said its net loss was expected to balloon to about 160 billion won for calendar 1996 from a loss of 126.2 billion in 1995.
The two companies have so far denied they are negotiating for any takeover.
